_comment: PvP (`pvp`, worlds created with it): a player may send an army to attack another player's village (orders `attack` to plunder it, `raze` to burn it to a ruin if they win; a refugee camp is only plundered). A village is safe from other players for `pvp.protectionHours` game hours after it is founded (divided by world speed). The fight is resolved at once when the army arrives: the village's garrison (in its stance, at home, with its hero and general) and the armies standing in it, behind its walls while they stand (each battering ram in the attacking army takes its `breach` share of the walls off), against the attacking army, round after round until one side breaks or the last round passes (then the defenders hold). The winner plunders `pvp.lootShare` of every store, as much as the army's units can carry (`carry`), or razes the village; either way the army then comes home. In a PvP world players' armies don't support each other's villages (caravans still go anywhere). Armies are troops out of their settlement, on the map. Garrisons (troops at home and in training) stay in their settlement and eat `supply.garrisonUpkeep` of their upkeep; they leave only by joining an army. `support` armies stand in a village and fight its battles; `reinforce` armies join the battle there and go back after; `harass` armies (at least `harass.minCavalryShare` cavalry) strike for one round with a bonus, take only `harass.lossFactor` of their losses, and ride back. A reinforcement arriving from a different side than the horde (at least `pincer.minAngle` degrees apart) gets a pincer bonus on its first round: `scale` x its size / the horde's size, at most `maxBonus`. Hammer and anvil: a reinforcement reaching a village whose walls still stand falls on the horde pinned against them, from whatever side it comes: on its first round `hammer.scale` x its size / the horde's size, at most `hammer.maxBonus`, in place of the pincer. An army carries its own grain: each of its units its own `supplyHours` (data/units.json) of its upkeep, and wagons their `supplyGrain`. On the march or on open ground it eats its full upkeep from it. Stationed in a settlement, a fort or a supply point it is quartered: it eats `quarters.upkeep` of its upkeep from that place's granary and its own grain keeps; the place feeds it down to its floor (by default `quarters.settlementFloor` of a settlement's grain storage, 0: to the last grain, as forts and supply points; the owner can set another), and once at the floor the army eats its own again. Setting off from such a place, it first fills up to its full supply, down to the same floor. Out of food, it marches `attrition.slowFactor` as fast; after `attrition.lossAfterHours` game hours it loses `attrition.lossShare` of each unit (rounded up) every `attrition.checkHours`, and after `attrition.lostAfterHours` it is lost altogether. A standing army answers battles within `respond.range` hexes of it (unless told not to): it marches there as a reinforcement and goes back to where it stood once the battle is over. Army groups (`groups`): a player keeps at most `maxPerPlayer`, each a name, a home settlement and a composition of at most `maxUnits` troops. Every `checkMinutes` game minutes a group whose army is not yet standing, or stands quartered in one of its owner's settlements, forts or supply points, has what it lacks trained: each unit in the owner's settlement closest to the army (to the home while there is none) that can train and pay for it, as much as can be paid for at once. Trained, they march to the army and join it; while there is none they gather at the home as the group's army.
